body.name: Studio
body.description: Build, publish, install and manage the organisation's applications. Its App Store section lists every application.

permissions.label: Open Studio
permissions.description: Allows opening Studio and its App Store.

flows.description: Removes an installed application, keeping its data or, after a typed confirmation of its name, deleting the data as well.

literal.value: Its pages and launcher entry leave this organisation and its roles stop granting access. By default its data is kept, so installing it again brings the data back. Ticking the box below deletes the data as well, for good: everything listed goes.
The application and all of its data were deleted.
The application was not removed: you may not delete its data, or its state changed. Nothing was deleted; check it in the list.
The application could not be removed with its data. Check its state in the list before trying again.
The application was removed. Its data is kept; install it again to bring it back.
The installation changed while you were reviewing it. Choose Remove again.
You cannot remove this application with your current authority.
The removal could not be confirmed. Check the application in the list before trying again.

Only installed ordinary applications can be removed, and you need permission to manage applications.

flows.description: Deletes an application that is not installed, with its definition, versions, roles and any data it holds, after a typed confirmation of its name.

literal.value: This deletes the application for good: its definition, every version, its roles and everything below. It cannot be undone.
The application was not deleted: you may not delete it, or its state changed. Nothing was deleted; check it in the list.

Only an application that is not installed can be deleted, and you need permission to manage applications.
The application could not be reviewed. Try again shortly.

flows.description: Creates an application from a name, a description and an optional key; it starts as a draft that is opened from the list.

literal.value: Name it and say what it is for. It starts as a draft you open with Edit in Studio.
The application was created as a draft. Open it with Edit in Studio, add pages and data, then publish it.

flows.description: Publishes the saved draft as the next version of the application, with a release note.

literal.value: Publishing makes this the version organisations can install or upgrade to. The saved draft is what is published.
